inventions.description: Surgical masks made of cloth were developed in Europe by physicians Jan Mikulicz-Radecki at the University of Breslau and Paul Berger in Paris, as a result of increasing awareness of germ theory and the importance of antiseptic procedures in medicine.

inventions.title: Plastic
inventions.description: Hans von Pechmann synthesizes polyethylene, now the most common plastic in the world.

inventions.title: Iron
inventions.description: Waldemar Jungner invents the rechargeable nickel-cadmium battery (NiCd) as well as the nickel-iron electric storage battery (NiFe) and the rechargeable alkaline silver-cadmium battery (AgCd)
inventions.significance: A common metal that made tools and weapons cheaper than bronze in many regions.

inventions.title: vacuum cleaner
inventions.description: The first motorized cleaner using suction, a powered "vacuum cleaner", is patented independently by Hubert Cecil Booth and David T. Kenney.

inventions.title: Ægidius Elling
inventions.description: The first successful gas turbine is invented by Ægidius Elling.

inventions.title: Glass
inventions.description: Édouard Bénédictus invents laminated glass.

inventions.title: diode
inventions.description: The Fleming valve, the first vacuum tube and diode, is invented by John Ambrose Fleming.

inventions.title: Plastic
inventions.description: Leo Baekeland invents bakelite, the first plastic made from synthetic components.

inventions.title: René Lorin
inventions.description: The tuyères thermopropulsives after 1945 (Maurice Roy (fr)) known as the statoreacteur a combustion subsonique (the ramjet)Anthony Roux (2 July 2009) Simulation aux Grandes Echelles d'un statoréacteur , p.15, University of Toulouse, "...La propulsion par statoreacteur a été inventée par le francais René Lorin en 1907 et decrite pour la ´

inventions.title: Cellophane
inventions.description: Cellophane is invented by Jacques E. Brandenberger.

inventions.title: Haber process
inventions.description: Fritz Haber invents the Haber process.

inventions.title: particle detector
inventions.description: The cloud chamber, the first particle detector, is invented by Charles Thomson Rees Wilson.

inventions.title: Bergius process
inventions.description: The Bergius process is developed by Friedrich Bergius.

inventions.title: Kaplan turbine
inventions.description: The Kaplan turbine is invented by Viktor Kaplan.

inventions.title: Eugène Brillié
inventions.description: The first operational military tanks are designed in Great Britain and France. They are used in battle from 1916 and 1917 respectively. The designers in Great Britain are Walter Wilson and William Tritton and in France, Eugène Brillié. (Although it is known that vehicles incorporating at least some of the features of the tank were designed in a number of countries from 1903 onward, none reached a practical form.)

inventions.title: Stainless steel
inventions.description: Harry Brearley invents a process to create Martensitic stainless steel, initially labelled Rustless Steel, later marketed as Staybrite, and AISI Type 420.

inventions.title: silicon
inventions.description: The Czochralski process, widely used for the production of single crystal silicon, is invented by Jan Czochralski.

inventions.title: crystal oscillator
inventions.description: The crystal oscillator is invented by Alexander M. Nicolson using a crystal of Rochelle Salt although his priority was disputed by Walter Guyton Cady.

inventions.title: Kaiser-Wilhelm-Institut für Kohlenforschung
inventions.description: The Fischer–Tropsch process is developed by Franz Fischer and Hans Tropsch at the Kaiser-Wilhelm-Institut für Kohlenforschung.
inventions.wikipediaTitle: Max Planck Institute for Coal Research

inventions.title: liquid fueled rocket
inventions.description: Robert H. Goddard launches the first liquid fueled rocket.

inventions.title: Television
inventions.description: John Logie Baird demonstrates the world's first live working television system.

inventions.title: Three-point hitch
inventions.description: Harry Ferguson, patents the Three-point hitch equipment linkage system for tractors.

inventions.title: quartz clock
inventions.description: The quartz clock is invented by Warren Marrison and J.W. Horton at Bell Telephone Laboratories.

inventions.title: Jet engine
inventions.description: Frank Whittle formally submitted his ideas for a turbo-jet engine. In October 1929, he developed his ideas further. On 16 January 1930, Whittle submitted his first patent (granted in 1932).

inventions.title: Penicillin
inventions.description: Penicillin is first observed to exude antibiotic substances by Nobel laureate Alexander Fleming. Development of medicinal penicillin is attributed to a team of medics and scientists including Howard Walter Florey, Ernst Chain and Norman Heatley.
inventions.significance: The first widely used antibiotic opened modern infectious-disease medicine.

inventions.title: Television
inventions.description: Philo Farnsworth demonstrates the first practical electronic television to the press.

inventions.title: ball screw
inventions.description: The ball screw is invented by Rudolph G. Boehm.

inventions.title: Phase-contrast microscopy
inventions.description: The Phase-contrast microscopy is invented by Frits Zernike.

inventions.title: Supersonic combusting ramjet
inventions.description: The Supersonic combusting ramjet — Frank Whittle.

inventions.title: Microscope
inventions.description: The electron microscope is invented by Ernst Ruska.
inventions.significance: Revealed a living world below the limit of the unaided eye.

inventions.title: Radio
inventions.description: FM radio is patented by inventor Edwin H. Armstrong.
inventions.significance: Information without wires. News, entertainment, and later digital data followed.

inventions.title: Steel
inventions.description: Harry C. Jennings Sr. and Herbert Everest, both mechanical engineers, invented the first lightweight, steel, folding, portable wheelchair with their "X-brace" design.
inventor: Harry C. Jennings Sr. and Herbert Everest

inventions.title: DuPont
inventions.description: Nylon, the first fully synthetic fiber is produced by Wallace Carothers while working at DuPont.

inventions.title: Computer
inventions.description: Z1, built by Konrad Zuse, is the first freely programmable computer in the world.

inventions.title: Soviet atomic bomb project
inventions.description: Nuclear fission discovered in experiment by chemists Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann and physicists Lise Meitner and Otto Robert Frisch. The German nuclear energy project was based on this research. The Tube Alloys project and, subsequently, the Manhattan Project and the Soviet atomic bomb project were influenced by this research.

inventions.title: Computer
inventions.description: John Vincent Atanasoff invented the first electronic digital computer

inventions.title: defibrillator
inventions.description: G. S. Yunyev or Naum Gurvich invented the electric current defibrillator

inventions.title: Microwave oven
inventions.description: John Randall and Harry Boot would develop the high power, microwave generating, cavity magnetron, later applied to commercial Radar and Microwave oven appliances.

inventions.title: nuclear devices
inventions.description: Pu-239 isotope (isotope of plutonium) a form of matter existing with the capacity for use as a destructive element (because the isotope has an exponentially increasing fissile decay) within nuclear devices — Glenn Seaborg.

inventions.title: Polyester
inventions.description: Polyester is invented by John Rex Whinfield and James Dickson.

inventions.title: Nuclear reactor
inventions.description: Enrico Fermi developed the nuclear reactor and created the first controlled nuclear chain reaction
inventions.significance: A controlled chain reaction showed that nuclear energy could be harnessed, for power as well as weapons.

inventions.title: Wernher von Braun
inventions.description: The V-2 rocket, the world's first long range ballistic missile, developed by engineer Wernher von Braun.

inventions.title: atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
inventions.description: The atomic bomb is developed by the Manhattan Project and swiftly used in August 1945 in the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
inventions.wikipediaTitle: atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

inventions.title: microwave oven
inventions.description: Percy Spencer, while employed at Raytheon, would patent a magnetron based microwave oven.

inventions.title: Science
inventions.description: Willard Libby began his work on radiocarbon dating. He published his paper in 1946, a second paper in Science in 1947. Libby and James Arnold succeeded with the radiocarbon dating theory after results were published in Science in December 1949.

inventions.title: ejector seat
inventions.description: James Martin invents the ejector seat, inspired by the death of his friend and test pilot Captain Valentine Baker in an aeroplane crash in 1942.

inventions.title: Holography
inventions.description: Holography is invented by Dennis Gabor.

inventions.title: hydraulic fracturing
inventions.description: Floyd Farris and J.B. Clark (Stanolind Oil and Gas Corporation) invents hydraulic fracturing technology.

inventions.title: Transistor
inventions.description: The first transistor, a bipolar point-contact transistor, is invented by John Bardeen and Walter Brattain under the supervision of William Shockley at Bell Labs.
inventions.significance: A solid-state switch made electronics small, reliable, and mass-producible — the seed of the digital revolution.

inventions.title: National Bureau of Standards
inventions.description: The first atomic clock is developed at the National Bureau of Standards.

inventions.title: Steel
inventions.description: Basic oxygen steelmaking is developed by Robert Durrer. The majority of steel manufactured in the world is produced using the basic oxygen furnace; in 2000, it accounted for 60% of global steel output.

inventions.title: Springer Science+Business Media
inventions.description: The Toroidal chamber with axial magnetic fields (the Tokamak) is developed by Igor E. Tamm and Andrei D. Sakharov.

inventions.title: video game
inventions.description: Bertie the Brain, debatably the first video game, is displayed to the public at the Canadian National Exhibition.

inventions.title: Glass
inventions.description: The float glass process is developed by Alastair Pilkington.

inventions.title: thermonuclear weapon
inventions.description: The first thermonuclear weapon is developed.

inventions.title: video tape recorder
inventions.description: The first video tape recorder, a helical scan recorder, is invented by Norikazu Sawazaki.

inventions.title: Telephone
inventions.description: Invention of the solar battery by Bell Telephone scientists, Calvin Souther Fuller, Daryl Chapin and Gerald Pearson capturing the Sun's power. First practical means of collecting energy from the Sun and turning it into a current of electricity.
inventions.significance: Speech at a distance collapsed the time of conversation. Several inventors worked on the problem; Bell received a key 1876 patent.

inventions.title: hovercraft
inventions.description: The hovercraft is patented by Christopher Cockerell.

inventions.title: Malcom McLean
inventions.description: The intermodal container is developed by Malcom McLean.

inventions.title: polio vaccine
inventions.description: Jonas Salk received the license for his inactivated polio vaccine

inventions.title: Computer
inventions.description: The Logic Theorist computer program, the first "artificial intelligence program", was written and invented by Allen Newell, Herbert A. Simon, and Cliff Shaw.

inventions.title: IBM
inventions.description: The hard disk drive is invented by IBM.

inventions.title: Internet
inventions.description: The laser and optical amplifier are invented and named by Gordon Gould and Charles Townes. The laser and optical amplifier are foundational to powering the Internet.
inventions.significance: A general-purpose packet network became the substrate for almost every later digital invention.

inventions.title: Orbital satellite
inventions.description: The first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, is launched.
inventions.significance: The first artificial satellite opened the Space Age and proved that machines could stay in Earth orbit.

inventions.title: Personal computer
inventions.description: The first personal computer used by one person and controlled by a keyboard, the IBM 610, is invented by IBM.

inventions.title: Integrated circuit
inventions.description: The integrated circuit is independently invented by Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce.
inventions.significance: Putting many transistors on one chip made computers cheap enough to leave the laboratory.

inventions.title: Transistor
inventions.description: The MOSFET (MOS transistor) is invented by the Egyptian Mohamed Atalla and the Korean Dawon Kahng at Bell Labs. It is used in almost all modern electronic products. It was smaller, faster, more reliable and cheaper to manufacture than earlier bipolar transistors, leading to a revolution in computers, controls and communication.
inventions.significance: A solid-state switch made electronics small, reliable, and mass-producible — the seed of the digital revolution.

inventions.title: combined oral contraceptive pill
inventions.description: The first combined oral contraceptive pill becomes publicly available.

inventions.title: Laser
inventions.description: The first functioning laser is invented by Theodore Maiman.

inventions.title: robotic exoskeleton
inventions.description: First robotic exoskeleton

inventions.title: electronic cigarette
inventions.description: The first electronic cigarette is created by Herbert A. Gilbert. Hon Lik is often credited with its invention as he developed the modern electronic cigarette and was the first to commercialize it.

inventions.title: high-speed rail
inventions.description: Shinkansen, the first high-speed rail commercial passenger service.

inventions.title: DuPont
inventions.description: Kevlar is invented by Stephanie Kwolek at DuPont.

inventions.title: Touchscreen
inventions.description: E. A. Johnson of the Royal Radar Establishment developed the capacitive touch display or touchscreen

inventions.title: Internet
inventions.description: The NPL network followed by the ARPANET implement packet switching for data communication, drawing on the concepts and designs of Donald Davies, and Paul Baran. These are considered precursors to the modern Internet.
inventions.significance: A general-purpose packet network became the substrate for almost every later digital invention.

inventions.title: in vitro fertilization
inventions.description: 1978: Birth of the first child through in vitro fertilization (IVF), based on the research of Patrick Steptoe and Robert Edwards

inventions.title: pocket calculator
inventions.description: The pocket calculator is invented.

inventions.title: Public-key cryptography
inventions.description: Public-key cryptography is invented and developed by James H. Ellis, Clifford Cocks, Malcolm J. Williamson, Whitfield Diffie, Martin Hellman, Ralph Merkle, Ron Rivest, Adi Shamir, Leonard Adleman, et al.

inventions.title: disk drive
inventions.description: IBM developed and released the world's first floppy disk and disk drive.

inventions.title: Microprocessor
inventions.description: The first single-chip microprocessor, the Intel 4004, is invented. Its development was led by Federico Faggin, using his silicon-gate MOS technology. This led to the personal computer (PC) revolution.
inventions.significance: A computer on a chip made personal computing, embedded control, and later smartphones possible.

inventions.title: Salyut 1
inventions.description: The first space station, Salyut 1, is launched.

inventions.title: DNA
inventions.description: Herbert Boyer and Stanley Cohen developed genetic modification when they successfully modified DNA

inventions.title: Science
inventions.description: The first video game console, used primarily for playing video games on a TV, is the Magnavox Odyssey.

inventions.title: Graphical user interface
inventions.description: The first commercial graphical user interface is introduced in 1973 on the Xerox Alto. The modern GUI is later popularized by the Xerox Star and Apple Lisa.

inventions.title: Optelecom
inventions.description: The first fiber optic communication systems were developed by Optelecom.

inventions.title: Touchscreen
inventions.description: The first capacitive touchscreen is developed at CERN.

inventions.title: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
inventions.description: The lithium-ion battery is invented by M. Stanley Whittingham, and further developed in the 1980s and 1990s by John B. Goodenough, Rachid Yazami and Akira Yoshino. It has impacted modern consumer electronics and electric vehicles.
inventions.wikipediaTitle: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

inventions.title: Internet
inventions.description: The Transmission Control Program is proposed by Vinton Cerf and Robert E. Kahn, building on the work of other Internet pioneers, creating the basis for the modern Internet.
inventions.significance: A general-purpose packet network became the substrate for almost every later digital invention.

inventions.title: puzzle
inventions.description: The Rubik's cube is invented by Ernő Rubik which went on to be the best selling puzzle ever.

inventions.title: home automation
inventions.description: First general purpose home automation network technology, X10, was developed

inventions.title: Automobile
inventions.description: The first self-driving car that did not rely upon rails or wires under the road is designed by the Tsukuba Mechanical Engineering Laboratory.
inventions.significance: Powered personal vehicles remade cities, work, and the geography of daily life.

inventions.title: DNA
inventions.description: Dr Walter Gilbert and Frederick Sanger invented a new DNA sequencing method for which they won the Nobel Prize.

inventions.title: Satellite
inventions.description: The Global Positioning System (GPS) enters service. While not the first Satellite navigation system, it is the first to enter widespread civilian use
inventions.significance: Artificial satellites made planetary observation, navigation, and global communication routine.

inventions.title: Microvision
inventions.description: The first handheld game console with interchangeable game cartridges, the Microvision is released.

inventions.title: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone
inventions.description: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone (NTT) launched the first cellular network in Japan.

inventions.title: Prestel
inventions.description: Public dialup information, messaging and e-commerce services, were pioneered through CompuServe and RadioShack's MicroNET, and the UK's Post Office Telecommunications Prestel services.

inventions.title: Restriction Fragment-length Polymorphisms
inventions.description: Scientists Mark Skolnick, Ron Davis, Ray White, and David Botstein published their findings on a gene mapping tool using Restriction Fragment-length Polymorphisms (RFLP), that would have applications to identify heritable disorders, including some forms of cancer.

inventions.title: Toshiba
inventions.description: Flash memory (both NOR and NAND types) was invented by Fujio Masuoka while working for Toshiba. It was introduced to the public in 1984.

inventions.title: digital media player
inventions.description: Kane Kramer develops the credit card-sized, IXI digital media player.

inventions.title: reusable spacecraft
inventions.description: The first reusable spacecraft, the Space Shuttle undergoes test flights ahead of full operation in 1982

inventions.title: Swedish Post and Telecom Authority
inventions.description: Comvik, a Swedish telecommunications company, launched the first commercial automatic cellular system. However, according to the Swedish Post and Telecom Authority, the company launched an unlicensed automatic system. Comvik didn't receive a license to operate until December 1981, two months after the NMT system was launched.

inventions.title: Telephone
inventions.description: Televerket, a Swedish state-owned corporation, launched the Nordic Mobile Telephone (NMT) system.
inventions.significance: Speech at a distance collapsed the time of conversation. Several inventors worked on the problem; Bell received a key 1876 patent.

inventions.title: Computer
inventions.description: The first laptop computer is launched, the 8/16-bit Epson HX-20.

inventions.title: Television
inventions.description: Direct to home satellite television transmission, with the launch of Sky One service.

inventions.title: AT&T
inventions.description: Ameritech, now known as AT&T, commercialized the Bell System (its cellular network) in Chicago, Ill.

inventions.title: Stereolithography
inventions.description: Stereolithography is invented by Chuck Hull.

inventions.title: DNA
inventions.description: DNA profiling is pioneered by Alec Jeffreys.

inventions.title: Motorola
inventions.description: The first commercially available cell phone in the US, the DynaTAC 8000X, is created by Motorola.

inventions.title: Printing
inventions.description: Chuck Hull patents the stereolithography (SLA) process, also known as 3D printing

inventions.title: Excell PCT105
inventions.description: Technophone, a British mobile phone company, created the first pocket-sized cell phone, the Excell PCT105.

inventions.title: mp3
inventions.description: Karlheinz Brandenburg would publish the audio compression algorithms that would be standardised as the: MPEG-1, layer 3 (mp3), and later the MPEG-2, layer 7 Advanced Audio Compression (AAC).

inventions.title: World Wide Web
inventions.description: The World Wide Web is invented by computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee.
inventions.significance: A shared hypertext layer made the internet usable as a public information space.

inventions.title: Search engine
inventions.description: The first search engine, "Archie", was created by Alan Emtage, Bill Heelan, and Peter J. Deutsch at McGill University

inventions.title: sim card
inventions.description: The first sim card is developed by Munich smart-card maker Giesecke & Devrient

inventions.title: SunDisk
inventions.description: The first commercial flash-based solid-state drive is launched by SunDisk.

inventions.title: Bluetooth
inventions.description: First generation of Bluetooth is developed by Ericsson Mobile. A form of data communication on short distances between electronic devices

inventions.title: Hagenuk MT-2000
inventions.description: A Tetris variant on the Hagenuk MT-2000 device becomes the first mobile game

inventions.title: Smartphone
inventions.description: IBM Simon, the world's first smartphone, is developed by IBM. It had a touchscreen and the first built-in apps for a mobile device.
inventions.significance: A pocket computer with a network connection moved computing into everyday life.

inventions.title: compact disc
inventions.description: DVD is an optical disc storage format, invented and developed by Philips, Sony, Toshiba, and Panasonic. DVDs offer higher storage capacity than compact discs while having the same dimensions.

inventions.title: Bolt
inventions.description: Bolt and Six Degrees (1997) both become the first social media sites.

inventions.title: Internet
inventions.description: The Ciena Corporation, in partnership with Sprint, deployed the first commercial dense wavelength-division multiplexing system, which created the massive capacity of the Internet.
inventions.significance: A general-purpose packet network became the substrate for almost every later digital invention.

inventions.title: Myriad Genetics
inventions.description: Myriad Genetics released the BRACAnalysis, the first commercial genetic test for assessing the risk of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer.

inventions.title: Nokia 9000 Communicator
inventions.description: Mobile web was first commercially offered in Finland on the Nokia 9000 Communicator phone, and it was also the first phone with texting

inventions.title: capsule endoscopy
inventions.description: The first capsule endoscopy was performed, after being invented in the mid-1990s by Gavriel Iddan

inventions.title: Online App store
inventions.description: NTT DoCoMo launches i-mode, the first integrated Online App store for mobile phones

inventions.title: TiVo
inventions.description: The first digital video recorder (DVR), the TiVo, is launched

inventions.title: contraceptive patch
inventions.description: The Food and Drug Administration approved the first contraceptive patch

inventions.title: Android operating system
inventions.description: Development of the Android operating system for mobile devices

inventions.title: podcast
inventions.description: First podcast, invented by Adam Curry and Dave Winer

inventions.title: YouTube
inventions.description: YouTube, the first popular video-streaming site, was founded by Jawed Karim

inventions.title: cloud computing
inventions.description: Amazon pioneered cloud computing

inventions.title: Amazon
inventions.description: First Kindle e-reader introduced by Amazon

inventions.title: iPhone
inventions.description: Apple Inc. released the iPhone

inventions.title: blockchain
inventions.description: Satoshi Nakamoto develops the first blockchain.

inventions.title: Science
inventions.description: The first quantum machine was created by Aaron D. O'Connell

inventions.title: J. Craig Venter Institute
inventions.description: The first synthetic organism, Mycoplasma laboratorium is created by the J. Craig Venter Institute

inventions.title: Lidar
inventions.description: Solid-state Lidar technology was introduced, replacing mechanical scanning with electronic beam steering

inventions.title: humanoid robot
inventions.description: Introduction of Pepper, the first commercial humanoid robot

inventions.title: CRISPR
inventions.description: Discovery of CRISPR gene editing method

inventions.title: artificial pancreas
inventions.description: First commercially available artificial pancreas

inventions.title: SpaceX
inventions.description: First successful launch of a multi-use rocket by SpaceX

inventions.title: quantum computing
inventions.description: IBM launches IBM Q System One, its first integrated quantum computing system for commercial use.

inventions.title: GPT-3
inventions.description: OpenAI demonstrated an Artificial Intelligence model called GPT-3. The program was created to generate human-like responses when given prompts. Launched in 2022.

inventions.title: mRNA vaccine
inventions.description: The first mRNA vaccine to be approved by public health medicines regulators is co-developed by Pfizer and BioNTech for COVID-19, with the potential to treat other diseases and cancer
